s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with rash and lymphadenopathy in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
key_facts: 43-year-old man
Fever, chills, and headache
Painless ulcer on the prepuce one month prior to admission
Healing of the ulcer prior to development of fever and fatigue
Disseminated maculopapular rash on the trunk and extremities
Multiple unprotected sexual contacts over the past three months
HIV infection diagnosed 10 years ago
Undetectable viral load and CD4 count of 1144 cells/μL
Previous treatment with intravenous penicillin G for suspected otosyphilis
Ill-appearing but not dehydrated on examination
Painless enlargement of inguinal, axillary, and cervical lymph nodes
White-cell count of 63,300/mL with a lymphomonocytic predominance
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed 19 white cells with normal glucose and protein concentrations

shortlist.label: Secondary syphilis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of painless ulcer on the prepuce and previous treatment for suspected otosyphilis, along with current symptoms of fever, rash, and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Infectious mononucleosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of fever, fatigue, and lymphadenopathy, which are consistent with infectious mononucleosis, particularly in an immunocompromised host

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised status and symptoms of fever, headache, and lymphadenopathy, which can be seen in toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised status and symptoms of fever, fatigue, and lymphadenopathy, which can be seen in cytomegalovirus infection

shortlist.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of unprotected sexual contacts and symptoms of fever, rash, and lymphadenopathy, which are consistent with lymphogranuloma venereum

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a painless ulcer on the prepuce, which healed prior to the development of fever, fatigue, and a disseminated maculopapular rash, is consistent with the secondary stage of syphilis. The patient's previous treatment for suspected otosyphilis and the presence of painless lymphadenopathy also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: The patient's age and the absence of typical symptoms such as sore throat and exudative tonsillitis make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: The patient's CD4 count is high, and toxoplasmosis typically occurs in individuals with lower CD4 counts

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: The patient's undetectable viral load and high CD4 count make CMV infection less likely

rejected.label: Lymphogranuloma venereum
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not specifically suggest LGV, and the presence of a painless ulcer and rash are more consistent with secondary syphilis
